Report:

Candidate (captured text) vs acceptance criteria:

1. Signature & purity — `def summarize_quality(records)`, single module, no imports, no I/O, no mutation of input. Pass.
2. Non-list top level — `if not isinstance(records, list):` (line 20 of candidate) returns available=False with all nine counters zero. Pass.
3. List sets available=True, empty list yields all-zero counters — loop never runs, returned dict has available=True, counters 0. Pass.
4. Valid-row handling — dict check, then `record.get('outcome')`, `isinstance(outcome, str)`, membership in the 5-name set. Only exact string match counts; `counters[outcome] += 1` only for those five, so no unknown key is ever written. Pass.
5. invalid_records — non-dict rows (e.g. None) and non-string/unknown outcomes (e.g. `[]`, int) increment only invalid_records and `continue`; no hash of the value occurs (set membership on the string), so unhashable values cannot crash. Pass.
6. tasks/authored — tasks increments per valid row; authored increments for every valid outcome except not_run. Pass.
7. No fractions/percentages, no dedup, no coercion (no `str()` of outcome). Pass.
8. Example — [assisted_delivery, not_run, unmodified_delivery, None, {outcome:[]}]: tasks=3, authored=2, assisted=1, not_run=1, unmodified=1, rejected=0, incomplete=0, invalid=2, available=True. Matches. Pass.
9. Return dict contains exactly the required keys: available plus the eight integer counters. Pass.
